plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid, and bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks negative profit. With value $25, the optimal bid is exactly $25.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no benefit to shading my bid below value—it only risks losing profitable wins. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so, and I never overpay since the price is set by the second-highest bid. With no repeated rounds to exploit, truthful bidding is optimal here.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding below my value only risks losing profitable auctions, while bidding above risks negative profit. With no information suggesting otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $39, so I will bid exactly that amount.
